result.reason: The New York governing-law change reaches the preferred position, but the venue provision does not. It applies only to proceedings “not resolved by arbitration,” while the existing language still permits confirmation of an arbitral award in any court of competent jurisdiction, including in the adverse party’s federal district. Thus, New York County courts do not have exclusive jurisdiction as required. The redline is otherwise narrow and preserves the arbitration arrangement, but the carve-out and retained confirmation language undermine the stated venue position.
